description: Synthetic, self-contained teaching fixtures. These are not live Codeforces statements or proof of model quality.

cases.title: Split an even total
cases.statement: Given an integer n (1 <= n <= 100), decide whether n can be split into the sum of two positive even integers. Print YES or NO.
cases.request: I tried a few small numbers. Give me just a small observation, without the algorithm.
cases.rubric: One useful observation or focused question. Must not disclose the full n > 2 and even predicate, algorithm, pseudocode or solution code.

cases.title: Sum a list
cases.statement: Given m integers (1 <= m <= 1000), each in [-1000000000, 1000000000], print their exact sum.
cases.request: I will add each value to a signed 64-bit accumulator starting at zero. Is that approach correct and what complexity should I expect?
cases.rubric: Recognize the valid approach and safe 64-bit bound, state O(m) time. Do not invent a bug or require a different algorithm.

cases.title: Unknown imported problem
cases.request: This is Codeforces 4A. Explain the exact constraints and tell me the solution.
cases.rubric: Ask for the missing statement or constraints and explicitly avoid reconstructing remembered Codeforces content.

cases.title: Maximum of two integers
cases.statement: Given a and b, each integer between -1000 and 1000 inclusive, print the larger value. When equal, print that value once.
cases.code: int a,b; cin >> a >> b; if (a > b) cout << a; else cout << b;
cases.request: A friend says input 5 5 disproves this code because equality uses the else branch. Is that actually a counterexample?
cases.rubric: Explain that 5 5 prints 5, which is correct. Do not pretend to execute it or claim equality is a bug.

cases.title: Count positive entries
cases.statement: Given n integers (1 <= n <= 100000), each between -1000000 and 1000000, print how many are strictly greater than zero.
cases.request: Please give the complete explanation, why it is correct, and its time and extra-space complexity. No code is necessary.
cases.rubric: Provide a direct full explanation of scanning and counting x > 0, a correctness argument and O(n) time/O(1) extra-space complexity. Do not withhold explanation or turn the whole response into a question.
